questions.text: What does a __proto__ key do in an object literal?
options: It sets [[Prototype]] and is not stored as an own property
It creates an ordinary own property whose value is the prototype
It copies the prototype’s keys into the new object
It changes the prototype of Object.prototype

questions.text: How is a computed ['__proto__'] key different from writing __proto__: proto in a literal?
options: Both forms do the same thing
A computed name is an ordinary own key. It does not change [[Prototype]]
The computed key sets the prototype, and the short form creates a property
The computed key removes Object.prototype

questions.text: Does writing to the constructor property change the result of instanceof?
options: Yes, instanceof compares obj.constructor with the function
Yes, but only when the property is enumerable
No. instanceof looks for Constructor.prototype in the chain and does not read the constructor property
instanceof looks at constructor and ignores the chain

questions.text: What does Symbol.hasInstance change for the right-hand operand of instanceof?
options: Nothing: instanceof always walks [[Prototype]]
The method changes the left operand’s prototype
The method runs only for class
That method replaces the ordinary chain check

questions.text: The literal { __proto__: null } still receives the Object.prototype chain.
The assignment obj.__proto__ = proto creates an own __proto__ property.
For class B extends null, the object B.prototype does not have Object.prototype in its chain.
An async function has a prototype property, like an ordinary function.
Which two links does class B extends null create?
questions.answer: B.prototype’s [[Prototype]] is null. The function B’s [[Prototype]] is Function.prototype.

questions.text: What does Object.prototype.toString.call return for a null-prototype object with no @@toStringTag?
What happens when a proxy’s setPrototypeOf trap returns false?
Why does Object.setPrototypeOf throw on a frozen object?
questions.answer: The object is non-extensible, so its [[Prototype]] can no longer be changed.

questions.text: Where does new take the prototype for a function wrapped with bind?
options: From the target function. The bound function itself has no prototype property
bind creates its own prototype and new uses that
new is always forbidden for a bound function
The prototype becomes the this that bind fixed

questions.text: Why can the [[Prototype]] of Object.prototype not be changed?
options: It can: the next link becomes the object you pass
It is an immutable prototype exotic object. Object.setPrototypeOf throws a TypeError
The ban exists only in strict mode, otherwise the prototype changes
The constructor property changes, not the chain

questions.text: How do you create an own property over an inherited one with writable: false?
options: Assignment is enough in any mode
You have to delete the property from the prototype
Object.defineProperty on the object itself. Ordinary assignment does not do this
No operation can shadow that property

questions.text: Why does Object.hasOwn stay reliable when hasOwnProperty is overridden?
options: It deletes the foreign hasOwnProperty first
It calls hasOwnProperty from Object’s prototype
It compares the key with the string constructor
It does not look up a method on the object and does not call a property from the chain

questions.text: An ordinary function has [[Prototype]] equal to Function.prototype.
In strict mode, Box.prototype = {} on a class throws a TypeError.
A property written on Object.prototype becomes visible on ordinary objects.
Object.getOwnPropertyNames also lists inherited names.
What does a sloppy assignment to an inherited property with writable: false do?
questions.answer: It changes nothing. No own property appears, and the prototype value stays. In strict mode the same step throws a TypeError.

questions.text: What does 'toString' in Object.create(null) return?
questions.answer: false. Object.prototype is not in the chain, so that name is absent.

questions.text: Does an ordinary read of proxy.n use the getPrototypeOf trap?
questions.answer: No, when there is no get trap. The read goes through the target and the target’s own prototype.

questions.text: What does an async function lack, compared with an ordinary function, regarding prototypes and new?
questions.answer: Its own prototype property. Calling it with new throws a TypeError.

questions.text:
const arrow = () => {};
console.log(Object.hasOwn(arrow, 'prototype') ? 1 : 0);
How does the in operator differ from for...in for a non-enumerable inherited name?
options: in sees that name. for...in skips it
Both skip it
Both show it
for...in sees it, and in returns false

questions.text: Does the in operator see a private field #n?
options: Yes, if you evaluate '#n' in obj
No. A private field is not a string key on the prototype chain
Yes, because the field lives on prototype
Yes, but only inside the class

questions.text: What stays fixed when a method that uses super is copied onto another object and called?
options: super starts the search at the new object
Both super and this come from the home object
The super search still starts at the home object’s prototype. this becomes the new receiver of the call
Such a method cannot be called from another object

questions.text: What part of the prototype machinery is missing on an arrow function?
options: The [[Prototype]] link to Function.prototype
The ability to be an object method
The closure over outer variables
Its own prototype property. An arrow cannot be called with new

questions.text: Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor sees a descriptor that lives only on the prototype.
JSON.stringify includes enumerable inherited keys.
Object spread copies enumerable inherited keys.
The third argument of Reflect.get becomes this inside a getter.
What does map return for an Array subclass when Symbol.species was left at the default?
questions.answer: An instance of that subclass. The default species is the constructor itself.

questions.text: What is the [[Prototype]] of the iterator returned by calling a generator function?
questions.answer: The prototype object of that generator function.

questions.text: What is the [[Prototype]] of Function.prototype?
Is a bound function an instance of Function?
questions.answer: Yes. Its [[Prototype]] is Function.prototype, even though it has no prototype property of its own.

questions.text: How does Symbol.species affect map on an Array subclass?
options: map builds the result with the species constructor, not always with the same subclass
species changes the prototype of the original array
species disables Array.prototype methods
map ignores species and always returns an Array

questions.text: Which internal operation does instanceof read, and what does that mean for a proxy?
options: [[Get]] of the constructor key
[[GetPrototypeOf]]. A getPrototypeOf trap can make instanceof true
[[OwnPropertyKeys]] of the left operand
A proxy has no effect on instanceof

questions.text: Where does Object.prototype.toString read @@toStringTag from?
options: Only among the own keys of Object.prototype
From the constructor name in the source text
It looks for it along the chain of the object it was called for
From the species property

questions.text: What does a strict assignment to an inherited getter with no setter do?
options: It creates an own property and hides the getter
It installs a default setter on the prototype
It changes the getter’s result to the assigned value
It throws a TypeError. No own property is created, and the getter still returns the previous value

questions.text: The third argument of Reflect.set can become the setter’s this even when the setter lives on another object.
Calling toString as a method on Object.create(null) throws a TypeError.
An own property named __proto__ shadows the getter from Object.prototype.
Object.create(Box.prototype) produces an object for which instanceof Box is true, even though the constructor did not run.
What does Object.setPrototypeOf return when the prototype change succeeds?
questions.answer: The same object that was passed in.

questions.text: Why does delete Box.prototype throw in strict mode when Box is declared with class?
questions.answer: A class’s prototype property is non-configurable. It cannot be deleted.

questions.text: Where is a private field stored relative to the prototype?
questions.answer: In an internal slot of the instance. It is not on prototype, and the string key '#n' does not read it.

questions.text: Does the name prototype appear in Object.keys for class Box?
questions.answer: No. A class’s prototype property is non-enumerable, so Object.keys does not show it.
